# egauth

> Misuse-resistant authentication for Go. One validated composition object (`egauth.New`) and one
> deny-by-default route builder (`Auth.Routes`). No handler, cookie, issuer or gate is wired by hand.

AUDIT STATUS: egauth's security review to date is an AI-driven audit only; it has not had an independent third-party human security audit, and that risk is accepted for v1.0 — pin a reviewed commit, commission your own audit, or wait if that trade-off is unacceptable. "AI-audited" is not a synonym for "audited". Full status, scope, and escape hatch in `AUDIT.md`.

module: `github.com/JLugagne/egauth` · Go 1.26+ · License MIT · status: pre-1.0 (API settling; AI-audited, no third-party human audit yet)
install (core): `go get github.com/JLugagne/egauth`
install (PostgreSQL stores, separate module): `go get github.com/JLugagne/egauth/adapters/pgx`

Machine-readable reference lives in `.llms/`. Authoritative API: `go doc -all github.com/JLugagne/egauth`.

## Start here

- [Architecture](.llms/architecture.md): composition object, packages, layering, why misuse is hard. READ FIRST.
- [Recipes](.llms/recipes.md): the compiled examples (memory service, routes, facade, PostgreSQL, v0.16 upgrade).
- [Configuration](.llms/config.md): every `egauth.Config` field, modules, what `New` checks, opt-outs.
- [Reference application](examples/fullstack): password, magic link, passkey, TOTP, self-delete and API keys on `New` and `Routes`. Run: `go run github.com/JLugagne/egauth/examples/fullstack@latest`.

## Conventions for LLMs using egauth

- Build one `egauth.Config`, call `egauth.New`, then declare every route on `Auth.Routes()` and serve the handler `Build` returns at the root. Do not register egauth endpoints on your own mux.
- Pick the verb by who may call: `Protect` (human session), `Optional` (anyone, principal may be anonymous), `ProtectAPI` (API key kinds), `Public`.
- Handlers take the principal as an argument; there is no context accessor.
- Administration goes through `Auth.Accounts`, `Auth.Tenants` and `Auth.APIKeys`, which check authorization themselves. Background work uses `Auth.System`.
- Weakening a default is only possible through `egauth.InsecureOptOuts`, each field with a reason.
- Link, code and revert-link fields of delivery messages are working credentials: read them in the deliverer, never log them.
- Tests use `memstore.New` and `egauthtest`; production uses `pgxstore.New` after `pgxstore.Migrate`.
